label: Mistral Vibe
description: One conversation with Mistral Vibe, Mistral AI's coding agent: three conversations are three nodes. Wire `agent` and `stream` into an AskAgent and talk to it in a Loop; end the loop with a CloseBus on `stream`, which ends this node's part of the run. With no `computer`, Mistral Vibe runs on your machine (a local install only) with your own login, working in `folder`, from your own install of `vibe-app-server` when there is one on PATH; when there is none, weft installs Mistral Vibe itself, once, into a folder of its own shared by every program on the machine. With a `computer` wired, it is installed and run inside that computer, which a cloud install needs, and it logs in with the connection on `access`. Its model sees your program's tools under their own names. A program tool named `ask_user_question`, `todo`, `cron` or `unified_harness_scratchpad` takes the place of Mistral Vibe's own tool of that name, which is turned off for the conversation; Mistral Vibe keeps `bash`, `read_file`, `write_file`, `edit`, `run_typescript`, `search_tool_functions`, `wait` and `skill` for itself, so a program tool with one of those names is refused. With a connection, `folder` is trusted in its own home, so its `AGENTS.md` and `.vibe/` are read. Its card shows what it is doing and a Start over button. What is exposed: the permission mode, the model, the effort, extra folders and the most model calls a turn makes.

inputs.name: computer
inputs.description: A Computer to run Mistral Vibe in. Left out, it runs on your machine, which only a local install has. Several agents may share one computer.

inputs.name: access
inputs.description: A MistralVibeAccess's `access`: a Mistral API key. Required with a `computer`. Left out on your machine, Mistral Vibe uses the login already on it.

inputs.name: folder
inputs.label: Folder
inputs.description: The folder Mistral Vibe works in. On your machine it is required, and must exist. In a computer it is a path inside the computer, its home folder when left out.

inputs.name: program
inputs.label: Program
inputs.description: On your machine: the Mistral Vibe program to run, when it is not the `vibe-app-server` on your PATH or the one weft installs (an install of your own, a version you keep for this). A path on your machine, so it cannot go with a `computer`.

inputs.name: permission
inputs.label: Permissions
inputs.description: What Mistral Vibe may do without asking. `ask`: every request it would put to a person comes out of AskAgent as a question. `accept_edits`: file edits go ahead, the rest asks. `bypass`: nothing asks, nothing is refused; for a computer, which is the wall around it.

inputs.name: model
inputs.label: Model
inputs.description: The model to use, as its `config.toml` names it. Left out, Vibe's default.

inputs.name: streamBy
inputs.label: Stream by
inputs.description: What goes out on `stream`: `message`, one event per whole message, tool use and result, so a run waiting on a long step sleeps; `token`, every piece of text as it is written too, which keeps the run awake while the agent writes.

inputs.name: effort
inputs.label: Effort
inputs.description: How much the model thinks before it answers. Left out, the model's default.

inputs.name: addDirs
inputs.label: Extra folders
inputs.description: Folders besides `folder` Mistral Vibe may read and change.

inputs.name: maxTurns
inputs.label: Most model calls
inputs.description: A whole number: the most model calls one turn may make. Left out, Vibe's default.

outputs.name: agent
outputs.description: The agent's handle: wire it into AskAgent's `agent`. Baked: made when the infra is started.

outputs.name: stream
outputs.description: Everything the agent does in this run, as AskAgent sends it. Wire it into every AskAgent of the loop, and into a CloseBus after the loop: the run's part of this node ends when it does.

then.message: MistralVibe '{id}' runs on the machine weft runs on, which a cloud install does not have; wire a Computer into `computer`.
MistralVibe '{id}' runs in a computer, where no login is waiting for it; give it a MistralVibeAccess on `access`.
MistralVibe '{id}' works on your machine, so it needs a `folder` to work in.
MistralVibe '{id}' has a `permission` it does not know; pick one of ask, accept_edits, bypass.
MistralVibe '{id}' has a `streamBy` it does not know; pick message or token.
MistralVibe '{id}' runs in a computer, where `program`, a path on your machine, means nothing; leave `program` out, the computer installs Mistral Vibe itself.
